title: MITOCHONDRIAL COMPLEX I DEFICIENCY, NUCLEAR TYPE 7

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that mitochondrial complex I deficiency nuclear type 7 (MC1DN7) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the NDUFV2 gene, which encodes the 24-kD subunit of complex I.

paragraphs.text: Mitochondrial complex I deficiency nuclear type 7 (MC1DN7) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutation in NDUFV2, a nuclear gene encoding a subunit of respiratory chain complex I. Affected individuals have been reported with early-onset hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, trunk hypotonia and encephalopathy, and others with Leigh syndrome without cardiac involvement (Benit et al., 2003; Cameron et al., 2015).

paragraphs.text: Benit et al. (2003) reported 3 affected sibs from a consanguineous family with complex I deficiency and early-onset hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with trunk hypotonia. The authors noted that, whereas mutations in a number of complex I subunit genes essentially result in neurologic symptoms, this NDUFV2 mutation was strikingly associated with cardiomyopathy.

paragraphs.text: In 3 sibs from a consanguineous family with complex I deficiency, early-onset hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and trunk hypotonia, Benit et al. (2003) identified a homozygous 4-bp deletion in intron 2 of the NDUFV2 gene (IVS2+5_+8delGTAA). The mutation was found by a combination of denaturing high performance liquid chromatography and sequence analysis. The mutation altered the consensus splice donor site of exon 2 and resulted in a 70% decrease in NDUFV2 protein and complex I deficiency.

paragraphs.text: In 2 sibs with complex I deficiency, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and brain atrophy, Cameron et al. (2015) identified compound heterozygous mutations in the NDUFV2 gene: the previously reported intronic mutation (c.IVS2+1delGTAA) and a novel 1-bp insertion (c.669_670insG) predicted to cause a frameshift (Ser224ValfsTer3). The mutations were found by whole-exome sequencing of fibroblast DNA from 1 sib. Subsequent investigation of 10 probands with complex I deficiency from different families revealed homozygosity for the c.IVS2+1delGTAA mutation in a second, consanguineous family in which 3 of 5 sibs were affected with Leigh syndrome without cardiac involvement.

agent.process_note: All four papers were available as abstracts only, and I read each one in full. The causal gene, NDUFV2, comes from Benit et al. (2003) and Cameron et al. (2015). Loeffen et al. (2001) is about NDUFS2, a different gene, so I left it uncited. Pagniez-Mammeri et al. (2009) screened NDUFV2 among 8 genes. Its abstract does not say which genes carried the defects found in 3 patients, so I could not credit it with an NDUFV2 mutation and left it uncited. Cameron et al. say the same genotype was reported in 'two families'. Only one of those (Benit) is in this folder, so I did not name the second. No reference data were supplied, so the intro has no NDUFV2 MIM number or chromosome location. The two papers name the intron 2 deletion differently: IVS2+5_+8delGTAA in Benit et al. and c.IVS2+1delGTAA in Cameron et al. I listed both names for that variant.
